items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: But it wasn’t really until I accidentally stumbled on and bought a record of his, and when I heard that it completely changed my life.

ctx.x: Did you hear George Lewis live?

I didn’t hear George Lewis live. Ironically I was 13 years old when he died. I wasn’t playing music then but that very same year that – he died on the last day of the year in 1968 but that very next year I started playing the clarinet. So I remember seeing his funeral on television and asking my mother, “Who is this George Lewis?” You know. So no I never got to hear him live. I got to play with a lot of people that played with him and they told me things about him. But it wasn’t really until I accidentally…

I don't know if this is a myth in my head, but when I was watching, just this morning I was watching a video of him and he would do a certain amount of, I call it “finger whacking.” And I know Kenny Davern would do this too, like he’d lift certain fingers up and really almost percussively play the instrument that way. And I was thinking well a classical clarinet teacher would not appreciate that. If they had a ruler they might slap your wrist. But I’m wondering if that physicalness of the finger movement is part…
